content: 1. The enzyme CYP3A4 is involved in the metabolism of erythromycin ethylsuccinate. Cimetidine can increase the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction to 50 mg twice daily should be considered. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 2. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate can increase the levels or effects of cinacalcet by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 3. Both citalopram and erythromycin ethylsuccinate can prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 4. Clarithromycin can increase the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both clarithromycin and erythromycin ethylsuccinate can prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 5. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate can increase the levels or effects of clomipramine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both clomipramine and erythromycin ethylsuccinate can prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 6. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate can decrease the levels or effects of clopidogrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, thereby reducing clopidogrel bioactivation. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate can increase the levels or effects of clozapine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both clozapine and erythromycin ethylsuccinate can prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 8. Cobicistat and erythromycin ethylsuccinate can mutually increase each other's levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Consider alternative antibiotics when cobicistat is coadministered with atazanavir or darunavir. 9. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate can increase the levels or effects of cobimetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If short-term use of moderate CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the cobimetinib dose to 20 mg. Resume the original dose after discontinuation of the inhibitor. 10. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate can increase the levels or effects of colchicine by inhibiting CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein (P-gp). Avoid or use an alternative drug. Colchicine is contraindicated with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. 11. Conivaptan can increase the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 12. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate can increase the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate can increase the levels or effects of cortisone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, cortisone can decrease the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 14. Both crizotinib and erythromycin ethylsuccinate can prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 15. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate can increase the levels or effects of cyclosporine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cyclosporine can also increase the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 16. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate can increase the effects of dalteparin by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 17. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate can increase the levels or effects of darifenacin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Darifenacin can also increase the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 18. Darunavir can increase the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 19. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate can increase the levels or effects of dasatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dasatinib can also increase the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate. This combination is contraindicated. 20. Both degarelix and erythromycin ethylsuccinate can prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 21. Both desflurane and erythromycin ethylsuccinate can prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 22. Both desipramine and erythromycin ethylsuccinate can prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 23. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate can increase the levels or effects of dexamethasone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, dexamethasone can decrease the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. DHEA (herbal) can increase the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate can increase the levels or effects of diazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 26. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate can increase the levels or effects of digoxin by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 27. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate can increase the levels or effects of diltiazem by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Diltiazem can also increase the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Consider an alternative to erythromycin in patients receiving diltiazem. 28. Both dofetilide and erythromycin ethylsuccinate can prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 29. Both donepezil and erythromycin ethylsuccinate can prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 30. Both doxepin and erythromycin ethylsuccinate can prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 31. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate can increase the levels or effects of dronedarone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dronedarone can also increase the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate. Both drugs can prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 32. Both droperidol and erythromycin ethylsuccinate can prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 33. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate can increase the levels or effects of edoxaban by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Dose adjustment may be required with strong P-gp inhibitors. 34. Efavirenz can decrease the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs can prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 35. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate can increase the levels or effects of elacestrant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 36. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate can increase the levels or effects of eletriptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Separate administration by 72 hours. 37. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate can increase the levels or effects of eliglustat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors are not recommended with eliglustat in poor or intermediate metabolizers. 38. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate can increase the levels or effects of eluxadoline by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Reduce the eluxadoline dose to 75 mg PO BID if coadministered with OATP1B1 inhibitors. 39. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate can increase the levels or effects of encorafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If concomitant use of a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the encorafenib dose by half. 40. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate can increase the effects of enoxaparin by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 41. Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and entrectinib can prolong the QTc interval. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate can also increase the levels or effects of entrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 42. Enzalutamide can decrease the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 43. Both epinephrine and erythromycin ethylsuccinate can prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 44. Both racemic epinephrine and erythromycin ethylsuccinate can prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 45. Erdafitinib can increase the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, separate administration by at least 6 hours. 46. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate can increase the levels or effects of ergotamine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 47. Both eribulin and erythromycin ethylsuccinate can prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If concurrent use is necessary, ECG monitoring is recommended. 48. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate can increase the levels or effects of erlotinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 49. Escitalopram can increase the toxicity of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 50. Eslicarbazepine acetate can decrease the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 51. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate can increase the levels or effects of estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 52. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate can increase the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 53. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate can increase the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 54. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate can increase the levels or effects of estropipate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 55. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate can increase the levels or effects of etonogestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 56. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate can increase the levels or effects of etravirine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, etravirine can decrease the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate. This combination is contraindicated. 57. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate can increase the levels or effects of everolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This combination is contraindicated. 58. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate can increase the levels or effects of felodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 59. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate can increase the levels or effects of fentanyl by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is necessary, monitor patients for respiratory depression and sedation, and consider fentanyl dose adjustments. 60. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate can increase the levels or effects of fentanyl (intranasal, transdermal, or transmucosal) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is necessary, monitor patients for respiratory depression and sedation, and consider fentanyl dose adjustments. 61. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate can increase the levels or effects of fesoterodine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 62. Fexinidazole can increase the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Fexinidazole inhibits CYP3A4, increasing the risk of adverse effects of CYP3A4 substrates. 63. Both fingolimod and erythromycin ethylsuccinate can prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
